title: Does Random Search Discover Task Experts? Revisiting Neural Thickets
abstract: arXiv:2611.01262v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Pretrained models are typically viewed as generalists, requiring bespoke post-training to achieve task-specific expertise. Gan & Isola (2026) recently proposed a striking alternative: that pretrained models lie in a dense neural thicket of task specialists, which can be surfaced with simple Gaussian weight perturbations. We examine this neural thicket of task-specific experts and identify several key findings that question this perspective. First, we find that the apparent lift of the best-of-N selected perturbation decays quickly with selection-set size m, strongly suggesting overfitting to the selection questions. In fact, for 10 of the 12 model-task pairs we study, a simple null model of pure selection noise predicts more than 75 percent of the top expert's reward lift. translated_title: 随机搜索能否发现任务专家？重新审视神经灌木丛
translated_abstract: 预训练模型通常被视为通才，需要定制化的后训练才能获得特定任务的专业能力。Gan & Isola（2026）最近提出了一个引人注目的替代观点：预训练模型处于一个密集的“神经灌木丛”之中，其中蕴含着任务专家，可以通过简单的高斯权重扰动将其显现出来。我们研究了这种由任务特定专家构成的神经灌木丛，并识别出若干质疑这一观点的关键发现。首先，我们发现通过 best-of-N 选择得到的最优扰动所带来的表观提升随着选择集大小 m 的增加而迅速衰减，这强烈暗示了对选择问题的过拟合。事实上，在我们研究的 12 组模型-任务配对中，有 10 组的顶尖专家奖励提升超过 75% 可以由一个简单的纯选择噪声零模型所解释。其次，顶尖专家的优势在保留问题（held-out questions）上往往消失，或仅停留在未扰动预训练模型的运行间波动范围之内。第三，我们…
tldr: 本文质疑了“预训练模型中存在可通过随机权重扰动发现的任务专家”这一观点，发现所谓的专家提升大部分可由选择噪声的过拟合解释，且在保留问题上优势往往消失或落入模型本身的运行波动范围内。
en_tdlr: This paper challenges the claim that pretrained models harbor task experts discoverable via random Gaussian weight perturbations, showing that the apparent expert gains are largely explained by overfitting to selection noise and vanish or fall within run-to-run variability on held-out questions.
